4_frames_reused_or_reloaded.correction: the first version of this stage claimed reuse was IMPOSSIBLE because splicing changes the hash. The test written to prove it went GREEN. That is true through the CUT day and false through the LAST COMPLETE day, where the appended bars sit above the cut and both frames hash the same prefix. Reuse WOULD have worked.
why_reload_anyway: the parquet is what the resume path reads, so fingerprinting it IS the contract rather than being equal to it by an argument about what the join touches
the closing slot holds only its own sleeve's instruments (sleeve_frames is called with one sleeve), so reuse would checkpoint 4 at the Swing close and 1 at NKD, never all 5 from one place
6s against 221s of headroom buys the simpler seam and leaves observe_live_slot's return shape alone
4_frames_reused_or_reloaded.pinned: a test asserts the two are interchangeable under the derived-day rule; it goes red the day the join starts rewriting history below the cut

5_measured_cost_and_headroom.share_of_budget: about 2%, and it lands on ONE slot per sleeve

6_fails_closed_on_open_book_without_entr.mirror_case: entries carry a position and the book says flat -> checkpoint_book_disagrees_with_entries

7_strategy_or_backtest_identity_changed.proof: sleeve_identity hashes identical before and after a write, both directions; the hash that lands in the entry is that same hash; checkpoint_frames imports no signal, rule or gate module (AST-checked)

part_b_writer_and_frames.what_the_closing_slot_holds: src.sleeve_frames(...)[sleeve] - the JOINED frames (parquet history + today's broker bars). JoinedFrame keeps only the joined result; the parquet is not retained. They are in scope at the close and dropped at observe_live_slot's return boundary.

parquet_state_at_a_1555_close.MES: newest day 2026-08-25 last bar 13:44; previous day 2026-08-24 last bar 23:59
parquet_state_at_a_1555_close.MNKD: newest day 2026-08-25 last bar 13:45; previous day 2026-08-24 last bar 23:59

the_measurement_that_decided_the_design.mechanism: the daily append runs at 13:45 ET, so the next append BACKFILLS today's afternoon - bars that sit BELOW the cut a fingerprint through today uses
the_measurement_that_decided_the_design.conclusion: an entry naming the cut day is refused by every later resume with fingerprint_rowcount, a code that reads like data corruption

part_b_writer_and_frames.design_adopted: last_complete_day(df) - the newest day the parquet has stopped filling, derived from the frame's own day index, returned tz-naive because fingerprint requires it

global_index/run_live_day_track1.py: checkpoint_frames(data_paths) -> ({inst: frame}, {inst: why not}); reports failures by name rather than raising, because a checkpoint writer must not stop a window closing

write_route_checkpoint: frames=None now means LOAD THEM; frames={} means deliberately none. They used to mean the same thing, which is exactly how the production call site wrote an empty checkpoint on every window
return value gains entry_count, instruments, last_day_by_inst, frames_unavailable
global_index/track1_bootstrap.py: checkpoint_entries gains optional last_day_by_inst; omitted, the cut day is used exactly as before, so the bootstrap path is byte-identical (asserted)
global_index/track1_shadow_acceptance.py: the companion book is the day proof in BOTH cases, not only the quiet one

stage_5zh_rule_replaced.old: when entries exist, their last_day must equal the judged day and the book is not consulted
stage_5zh_rule_replaced.why_wrong: a correct entry names the PREVIOUS trading day, so the rule would have failed every real checkpoint the writer can produce - including the first one
stage_5zh_rule_replaced.new: the book is the day proof in both cases; entries are asked only that their history is not from the future and not stale
stage_5zh_rule_replaced.live_evidence_re_judged: checkpoint check still OK for the quiet artefact; roska4_swing 2026-08-25 still PASSes; Calm/Stress/NKD still fail on their own grounds

not_fixed_here.finding: the route has no cross-day book
not_fixed_here.detail: observe_live_slot builds a fresh Track1Book per slot and never loads the persisted one; write_route_checkpoint synthesises a state with positions: [] when no book_state is handed to it. Today's book is a correctly-shaped 'nothing is held' marker, accurate only because nothing is held.
not_fixed_here.consequence: the open-position path is built and tested but NOT REACHABLE in production
not_fixed_here.what_stands_in_the_gap: the fail-closed guard - the day a position exists and the checkpoint does not record it, the audit says so instead of passing

tests.why: the one claim a fixture cannot support is a runtime-budget claim; the budget test asserts the frames it timed are over a million rows each, so it cannot pass on a toy

part_e_liveness.why: every changed module is imported by a SUBPROCESS - the scheduler spawns `python -m global_index.run_live_day_track1` for slots and `_run(argv)` for audits, and both pick up current source on the next launch. The dashboard reader was not touched, so the backend is unaffected.
part_e_liveness.timing_note: the next Track 1 window opened 4 minutes after this was written; restarting the scheduler then would have been the wrong trade for no gain
